text:
Evan: quick heads-up — onboarding sample app hitting auth retry loop on Android 14 emulators after ProGuard shrink. Repro steps in thread below, seems like okhttp Authenticator gets invoked twice and we end up with duplicate refreshes.

Sara: ugh. can you paste logs + okhttp client config?

Evan: logs: 
```
W/OkHttp: response for https://api.redwood.ai/token: code=401 message=Unauthorized
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, new token saved
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, but original call already retried -> 401 again
```
Client snippet: 
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor()) // attaches access token
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```

Mike: looks like a race where the interceptor attaches an old token while the authenticator is also refreshing, then the interceptor triggers another request that causes the authenticator again. On Android the thread scheduling + ProGuard/shrinker inlines something and makes timing worse.

Ashley: two quick fixes: 1) make AuthInterceptor check a shared atomic boolean that indicates an in-flight refresh and avoid re-attaching/stashing a retry while refresh in progress; 2) set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for auth flows so okhttp won't retry low-level at the same time. Also ensure TokenAuthenticator only triggers on responses with "WWW-Authenticate: Bearer" or similar, not every 401.

Mike: also watch out for using `synchronized` on Application/Activity scope — moving the token refresh to a single-threaded CoroutineScope helped us in another project. Eg: `refreshMutex.withLock { ... }`.

Evan: tried the mutex pattern + turning off retryOnConnectionFailure for the auth client, much better. Repro still exists on emulator sometimes (race window), but it fails far less. CI logs after change: 
```
[RUN] onboarding-sample - serial
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=def456)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete
I/OkHttp: retried request with new token -> 200
[PASS] onboarding-sample
```

Sara: nice. we should update sampleapp docs and add a small note in SDK docs about interceptor vs authenticator ordering + recommended patterns for Android (mutex/coroutine, avoid double-refresh). Could be a gotcha for customers.

Ashley: also flagged a ProGuard keep rule that was missing for the Token class; obfuscation was altering equals/hashCode which made AtomicReference comparisons weird. Add this in sampleapp proguard-rules.pro: 
```
-keep class com.redwood.sdk.auth.Token { *; }
```

Evan: added PR draft: `devex/disable-retry-auth-mutex` with tests and updated README in the sample app. CI run: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/2123 (android-ci)

android-ci: Build 2123 succeeded (emulator API 34, 3/3 instrumentation tests passed) :white_check_mark:

Mike: follow-ups: 1) add an e2e test that simulates concurrent 401s to catch regressions; 2) include a short note in the SDK migration guide about ProGuard and token model keep rules; 3) consider exposing a safeAuthClient() helper in the SDK that configures `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` + recommended timeouts.

Evan: agreed. I'll open tickets for 1+2 and a small RFC for the helper. Thanks all :thumbsup:
